alias: Purifier — run after the cat toilet
description: v3. Runs the corridor purifier after a cat visit for up to ~28 minutes, ending early ONLY if the PM2.5 sensor proved it is responsive (it rose after the visit) and then came back down. A sensor pinned at its floor gets no vote and the full window runs. Shutdown depends on a run-local fact, never on the ownership flag, so the flag cannot strand the fan on. A manual switch-off suppresses re-starts for a cooldown. Recovery fires on an automation RELOAD as well as a restart, because a reload also kills an in-progress run.

actions.note:
v3. Round 1 of review (review-20260920-2ca2) plus one finding the review could not have made, because it was observed live.

F9, THE RELOAD. Writing v2 reloaded the automation while a real run was in flight - a cat had used the box ten minutes earlier and v1 was mid-window. A reload kills the run exactly as a restart does, but it does NOT raise the homeassistant start event, so the recovery branch never fired and the fan was left on with the ownership flag set and nothing to clear it. Recovery now also triggers on the automation_reloaded event. This is the same class as P1 in the climate work: state that outlives the thing that was supposed to clean it up.

Recovery is gated on the OWNERSHIP FLAG ALONE, deliberately. v2 briefly used 'flag on OR fan on', which would have turned off a purifier a person had started by hand on every reload and every restart - taking control away from the operator, the thing this design exists to avoid. Flag-off-fan-on can no longer occur anyway, because ownership is claimed only after the fan is confirmed running.

F2, THE STRANDED FAN. Shutdown used to require the persistent flag, which made the 25-minute backstop conditional on the very state whose failure is the failure mode. It now turns on we_started, a RUN-LOCAL fact established by RE-READING the fan after commanding it - never assume a service call worked, the same interlock the climate loop uses before every actuating call.

F3/F1, THE SENSOR THAT TELLS US NOTHING. The early stop is armed only if PM2.5 rose above the floor after the visit. The operator's worry is a reading that is 'almost always at one'; if it is still at the floor after three minutes of fan then we have learned nothing, so it gets no vote and the full window runs. The old shape leaned on a subtlety - a numeric_state trigger does not fire when its condition already matches at attach - which gives the safe answer but should not be load-bearing.

F4, RE-IGNITING AFTER A MANUAL STOP. A manual switch-off is stamped and suppresses re-starts for 30 minutes, so the litter box cannot overrule a person who wanted quiet.

INSTRUMENTATION. input_text.purifier_last_run records one line per run: outcome, duration, PM before/after-settle/final, whether the sensor was responsive, and corridor temperature before and after. That last pair is the measurement that decides whether the purifier's motor heat biases the corridor reading enough to matter to the household average, and whether the corridor may ever join the mould check. Meant to be read after a few cycles and then removed.
